claim: Worktrees allow several branches to be checked out at separate paths while sharing one Git object database.
Unlike separate clones, worktrees can see local commits and branches from the other working directories without pushing them to a remote.
A reliable worktree creation script must restore needed ignored files and install dependencies because only tracked files are present initially.
Git does not allow one branch to be checked out in two worktrees at the same time.
Dexter usually limits himself to two concurrent agents and also uses worktrees to preserve tasks that he may resume later.
The demonstration uses agents that commit incremental work and a separate loop that checks their branches and merges new commits.
note: Observed as a live demonstration. The resulting code was not retained in the episode folder for independent verification.

claim: The speakers recommend naming worktrees by a stable convention and cleaning each one up after its branch is merged.
Standardizing parallel agent outputs makes progress easier to compare because each review checkpoint has the same shape.

The speakers warn that using worktrees for every research and planning step can create excess merging and context overhead, while parallel document variants can still be useful for deliberate comparison.
